judgment_methodology.method: Google's Rules of ML ("Rule #1: Don't be afraid to launch a product without machine learning") as the build/no-build judgment lens

planning_methodology.method: CRISP-DM phases (business understanding -> data understanding -> preparation -> modeling -> evaluation -> deployment)

deliverable_form.method: Model Card documenting intended use, training data, and evaluation metrics
deliverable_form.source: Mitchell et al., "Model Cards for Model Reporting," FAT* 2019; research.google/blog/introducing-the-model-card-toolkit-for-easier-model-transparency-reporting

feedback_methodology.method: Rules-of-ML review pass (rules 1-20, the "before machine learning" phase) applied before approving a new model path

review_methodology.method: CRISP-DM evaluation-phase sign-off against the business success criteria set at the planning phase

reference_resolution.rule: model_id must resolve to an actual model artifact or registry entry — no orphan references (issue-515 invariant 2).

recomputation.rule: verdict is recomputed from eval_data's current metrics, never a standalone asserted field.
recomputation.checked_by: TBD (follow-up — issue-521 out-of-scope note: per-role recomputation enforcement is a follow-up once evidence from real usage shows which roles need it)

quality_bar.verification_method: automated check that intended_use, training_data, and eval_data are all non-empty, plus a human-review-checklist pass confirming ethical_considerations is populated or explicitly stated as not applicable, per Mitchell et al.'s Model Cards field set
quality_bar.verified_source: Mitchell et al., 'Model Cards for Model Reporting' (FAT* 2019) — https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.03993 (primary source; intended_use, training_data, eval_data, and ethical_considerations are four of the paper's own nine named sections).

quality_bar.verification_method: human-review-checklist: does the proposal show a simple heuristic/non-ML baseline was considered and rejected with a stated reason, per Google Rules of ML rule #1?
quality_bar.verified_source: Martin Zinkevich, 'Rules of Machine Learning: Best Practices for ML Engineering,' Google — https://martin.zinkevich.org/rules_of_ml/rules_of_ml.pdf (primary source; Rule #1 'Don't be afraid to launch a product without machine learning' is verbatim in the document, with the heuristic-first rationale the criterion cites).

quality_bar.verification_method: human-review-checklist: do eval_data's reported metrics map explicitly to the business success criteria stated at CRISP-DM's business-understanding phase, not a generic accuracy/F1 number with no stated threshold?
quality_bar.verified_source: CRISP-DM 1.0 Step-by-Step Data Mining Guide (SPSS/Chapman et al. 2000), business-understanding phase defines 'business success criteria' as a named deliverable distinct from a generic accuracy/F1 number — consistent secondary confirmation via multiple practitioner writeups (e.g. https://www.datascience-pm.com/crisp-dm-2/). No stronger single canonical source exists beyond the original CRISP-DM consortium document; graded validated since the phase and its success-criteria artifact are the methodology's own defined terms, not a practitioner gloss.

quality_bar.verification_method: automated check (e.g. hash/ID-set comparison) that eval_data and training_data share no overlapping records
quality_bar.verified_source: No single named canonical source in the original spec; this is universal ML-methodology consensus (train/test leakage inflates reported performance), documented across many independent sources (e.g. Kapoor & Narayanan et al. lineage on leakage; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-022-01618-6 for a concrete inflation case). Kept as practitioner-consensus, automated hash/ID-set check as already specified.

use_when.board_condition: a model artifact is proposed for landing on the branch AND no ml-engineering record exists yet for that model_id
